# `silk/crypto/sm3`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Compute SM3 digests (GB/T 32905-2016), the hash of the Chinese commercial cryptography suite.

## When to use
Use [`Sm3`](#Sm3) where a protocol or format names SM3, such as SM2 signatures or the TLS 1.3
ShangMi suites of RFC 8998. Use SHA-256 elsewhere.

## Details
The streaming state does not allocate. Call `make`, `update`, and `finish`, or use `hash`. The
digest is 32 bytes.

## Examples
### Hash a message in parts
```silk
import silk.crypto.sm3 { Sm3 }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut state = Sm3.make()
  state.update(b"a")
  state.update(b"bc")
  let digest = state.finish()
  // SM3("abc") is 66c7f0f4...a8e0.
  if digest[0] != 0x66 || digest[31] != 0xe0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## See also
[RFC 8998](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8998.html) and the
[SM3 draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-sca-cfrg-sm3) describe the algorithm.

Import as `Sm3` with `import silk.crypto.sm3 { Sm3 }`.
